info.title: Release Notes API
info.summary: Add notes to Release Notes from anywhere: a terminal, a script or an app.
info.description:
Make a token in Release Notes under Settings, API tokens, and send it as `Authorization: Bearer rn_...`. An app can sign in instead, with OAuth for the resource /v1: the owner chooses the token it gets. Notes come from the owner, shown with “via <token name>”. With `media:write`, a note takes photos, recordings and PDFs, uploaded first to a signed form, and a new note can have a place. With the `upcoming` scope, a token keeps Upcoming dates too, and reads the reminders each morning carries. The guide is at /guide/api/.

Bodies are JSON in UTF-8, at most 256 KB, which holds the longest note with every character escaped. With `Accept: text/plain`, any answer is text instead: a line, or a line for each thing a list holds, and a note’s words as they are.

Every write but an upload form and Here takes an optional `Idempotency-Key`; its receipt answers the same request again for 7 days, sent through any token of the account. A write that counts toward a limit says where it stands in `RateLimit-*`; a replay counts nothing.

A day in UTC, an account may add 100 notes, make 200 other changes, save Upcoming 50 times and name 100 spots across its tokens, and upload 200 files with the web's; each token may read 2,000 times.

x-changes.summary: Odd bodies: POST /v1/notes reads a form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, as a Shortcut’s Form body sends it) as its text, date and written_at, when those are its only fields and text is one; any other form is still the words, and a multipart or media body is refused. A body may be 256 KB, room for the longest note with every character escaped. A note’s words lose control characters other than tab and newline, as from every channel, and a JSON body holding a lone surrogate escape is refused. A note’s place is kept as sent, its shape checked.

Moments: a new note can carry a `moment`, what an app picked for it (a workout, a song or podcast, steps, a feeling, an event, people, a reflection prompt) as typed values beside its words. GET /v1/notes/{date}/{id} returns it as kept, and the note.added activity row names its kinds, never its words.

The contract says what answers do: POST /v1/uploads and POST /v1/places/here take no Idempotency-Key, since neither keeps a receipt (a retry asks again); RateLimit headers come on a write that counts, not on a replay; and Accept: text/plain gives text, a line for each thing a list holds. Accept is read in full, so text/plain wins only where it outranks application/json. A token’s 404 and 405 answers say today’s version too, and a body naming another date or id than the path is invalid_request.

Which account and which token: GET /v1/me gives the account’s id, the same for every token of the account and never changing, and the token’s own id; each activity row a token writes from now names it by token_id. An Idempotency-Key now holds for the account: the same key sent through another of its tokens gets the first answer, and a different request under it is idempotency_mismatch.

Signing in: an app can get its token with OAuth (the authorization code with PKCE, for the resource /v1, with its own https or reverse-DNS callback), choosing among notes:write, media:write, upcoming and activity; the owner names the token, ticks its scopes and picks its expiry, and the answer is that token, with no refresh. The app can sign out at /oauth/revoke as well as DELETE /v1/token.

Files and places: with the media:write scope, a signed form for each photo, recording or PDF, and files on a new note or added to one this token wrote; and a new note’s place, from the city search or from Here, which names a device’s spot and the businesses near it.

Upcoming, with the upcoming scope: list the dates ahead, add, change and remove up to 50 at once (all or nothing, with a dry run), remove one, and read the reminders each morning carries for up to 31 days ahead, with when the email is due.
The first version: who the token is and the days ahead, text notes, tags and pinned tags, and the activity log.

get.summary: Today's version, the next 14 days' versions, and this token
get.description: What a client needs to show the version and fire reminders offline, without ever working out a version itself. The birthday is never sent. Any token may read it.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: You're 4.5.137 today.

post.description: A note in the owner's own voice, shown with “via <token name>” on the web. Hashtags in the text are its tags. A `text/plain` body is the note’s text alone, and so is a form that is not a `NoteForm`; a multipart body is refused. With neither `date` nor `written_at`, it files to today. With `uploads` (and the `media:write` scope) it takes those files, and then needs no text. A `place` is a city from `GET /v1/places` or the `place` from `POST /v1/places/here`, sent back as it came, and kept as sent: its shape is checked, not the place. A `moment` (since 1.6.0) keeps what an app picked for the note, a walk, a song or who was there, as values beside the words: the words are still the note, and the moment is shown, exported and deleted with it.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: Filed in 4.5.137.

get.summary: Read a note this token wrote
get.description: Its text and revision, so an app can pick up an edit made on the web.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: The note’s text.
A day in the account’s own time zone.

put.summary: Replace the text of a note this token wrote
put.description: From the revision the client read: a note changed since is a 409 `revision_mismatch` with its current `revision`. No history is kept.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: Changed in 4.5.137.
A day in the account’s own time zone.

delete.summary: Delete a note this token wrote

schema.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

post.summary: Add a paragraph to a note this token wrote

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: Changed in 4.5.137.
A day in the account’s own time zone.

post.summary: Add files to a note this token wrote
post.description: Uploads from `POST /v1/uploads`, each checked against the bytes that arrived, up to 20 files on a note in all. It counts as a change. A note takes each upload once; a write refused or lost before it lands leaves the uploads for a retry with the same Idempotency-Key.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: Changed in 4.5.137.
A day in the account’s own time zone.

post.summary: A signed form for one file
post.description: A photo, recording or PDF of up to 50 MB, its exact size given. Post the file to `url` as `multipart/form-data`, with every one of `fields` and then the file as `file`, within `expires_in` seconds, then name the upload in a note's `uploads`. An account takes 200 files and 2 GB a UTC day, with the web's. It has no receipt: a retry gets a new form, and an unused one expires.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: The upload’s id.

get.summary: Find a city by name, for a note’s place
get.description: The web’s city search. Send one of the answers as a note’s `place`, as it came.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: One line a city.

post.summary: Name the spot a device is at, for a note’s place
post.description: The city and neighbourhood, and the businesses Amazon Location finds within the accuracy (50 to 200 m), up to 6. Send `place` back as a note’s place, with `venue` set to one `nearby` name if the owner picks one; nothing is picked for them. An account names 100 spots a UTC day across its tokens. Nothing is kept until a note takes the place. It has no receipt: a retry asks again, and counts again.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: The spot’s names, then what is nearby.

get.summary: The tag row: pinned tags, then the most used lately
get.description: The pinned tags, then the tags used most in the last 30 days that aren't pinned, ties broken by last use. Any token may read it.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: #house #work #running

put.description: Up to 12 tags, normalized as note hashtags are ("#Running" is running), each once. The same pins show on the web and through every token.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: #house #work

get.summary: The activity log, newest first, without words
get.description: What came in, changed and went out. It never carries a mail subject, mail words, another sender or a settings value. An Upcoming row's title comes only with the `upcoming` scope.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The next older page: `next` from the answer before.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only rows newer than this one, an `id` the client has seen.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: One line a row: when, kind and token.

get.description: Every saved birthday, anniversary, trip and event, soonest first, with its next date and the line the email uses. A one-time date already over is left out and counted in `past_left_out`, since it still takes one of the account's 200.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: One line a date: its next date and its line.

post.summary: Add, change and remove up to 50 Upcoming dates at once
post.description: All or nothing: if any entry has a problem, nothing is saved and the error names it (`field` is like `change[2]`). A change replaces the saved date from the `revision` the client read; one changed since is a 409 `revision_mismatch`. A trip’s destination is text the city search knows, like "Paris, Texas". With `dry_run`, it checks everything and finds the cities but saves nothing, and counts as a read.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: Saved: 2 added, 1 changed, 0 removed.

get.summary: The reminders each morning carries, for the days ahead
get.description: Each day with a reminder due, from today: the reminders the morning email carries for dates with `email` on (all of them, where the email shows three), each with the email’s own `when` and `line`, and `send_at`, when that morning’s email is due. An app schedules them as notifications and reads again when it opens.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days from today, today included.

schema.description: With Accept: text/plain: One line a reminder: its day, when and line.

delete.description: From the revision the client read: a date changed since is a 409 `revision_mismatch`.
The token ends itself, as a sign-out does. Any token may.

token.description: An API token: rn_ and 43 more characters, shown once when it is made.

signIn.description: An app signing in: register at /oauth/register (a public client, with its own https or reverse-DNS callback), then the authorization code with PKCE (S256) and `resource` https://notes.yourversionnumber.com/v1. The owner names the token, ticks its scopes from those asked for and picks its expiry; the answer is that API token, with no refresh token. Discovery is at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/v1.

scopes.notes:write: Add notes, and change or delete the notes it adds
scopes.media:write: Add files to the notes it adds (only beside notes:write)
scopes.upcoming: Read and change Upcoming dates and their reminders
scopes.activity: Read the activity log, without any words from it

Idempotency-Key.name: Idempotency-Key
Idempotency-Key.description: Any 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters, new for each change. Sent again with the same request, through this token or another of the account’s, it answers the first result again; with a different request it is a 422.

Release-Notes-Version.description: Today's version, on every answer to a token.

RateLimit-Limit.description: The day’s limit for this kind of write.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the limit starts again, at midnight UTC.

Error.description: 400 invalid_request, 400 text_required, 400 date_out_of_range, 401 token_missing, 401 token_unknown, 401 token_revoked, 401 token_expired, 403 scope_required, 403 not_yours, 403 origin_refused, 404 not_found, 405 method_not_allowed, 409 revision_mismatch, 409 account_closing, 409 busy, 413 too_large, 422 idempotency_mismatch, 429 rate_limited, 503 unavailable

message.description: A sentence that says what to do next.

field.description: The field or header at fault.

revision.description: With revision_mismatch: the note’s current revision.

account.description: The account’s id: the same for every token of the account and never changing, so a client can tell whose account a token opens. It means nothing anywhere else. Since 1.4.0.

today.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

send_time.description: When the morning email goes, local time.

anyOf.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

days.description: 14 days from today; a birthday shows as a new major or minor version on its day.

date.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

id.description: This token’s id, which never changes and is never the token itself; activity rows it writes carry it as `token_id`. Since 1.4.0.

text.description: At most 20000 characters. Control characters other than tab and newline are dropped, and a lone surrogate escape is refused (since 1.7.0).

date.description: Any day from the birthday through today. Default: the day it was written.

written_at.description: When the words were typed, at most five minutes ahead. A note queued offline files to the day it was typed and is ordered by it.

NoteForm.description: A form, as a Shortcut’s Form body sends it, read as these fields when every name is one of them and `text` is there; any other form body is the words. Since 1.7.0.

text.description: At most 20000 characters. Control characters other than tab and newline are dropped, and a lone surrogate escape is refused (since 1.7.0).

date.description: Any day from the birthday through today. Default: the day it was written.

written_at.description: When the words were typed, at most five minutes ahead. A note queued offline files to the day it was typed and is ordered by it.

Moment.description: What an app picked for the note (Apple’s Journaling Suggestions, say), kept beside its words as it was sent: words trimmed and empty ones left out. A place visited is the note’s `place`, and photos are its `uploads`. Since 1.6.0.

MomentItem.description: One piece, by its `kind`. An unknown kind or field is `invalid_request`, naming it (`moment.items[2].distance_m`). Kinds: workout, song, podcast, played, steps, feeling, event, people, reflection.

name.description: The workout’s own name (“Yoga”), for one with no activity here.

oneOf.title: played
oneOf.description: Something listened to in another app.

hosted.description: Kept as false when not sent.

Uploads.description: Files posted to forms from `POST /v1/uploads`, each once. Needs `media:write`.

upload.description: The id the form came with.

name.description: The file’s name, shown with it; a long one is shortened.
The file’s name, which helps tell its type.

type.description: A photo, recording or PDF’s media type.
The type it was signed for: name the upload with it.

fields.description: Every one goes in the form, before the file.

expires_in.description: Seconds the form is good for.

DevicePlace.description: A spot, kept to six decimal places, with its names.

district.description: The neighbourhood, which names the note by default.

NotePlace.description: A city from `GET /v1/places`, or the `place` from `POST /v1/places/here`, kept as sent: its names, time zone and spot are checked for shape, and it is never looked up again.

text.description: At most 20000 characters. Control characters other than tab and newline are dropped, and a lone surrogate escape is refused (since 1.7.0).
At most 20000 characters. Control characters other than tab and newline are dropped, and a lone surrogate escape is refused (since 1.7.0).

date.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

files.description: How many files the note has.

token.description: The token’s name, as “via” shows it.

unlocked.description: Badges this note earned, only while Show badges is on, and never on a replay.

date.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

moment.description: The moment it was written with, as kept. Since 1.6.0.

last_used.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

UpcomingFields.description: A date as it is saved. A change sends every field again, as it should be.

date.description: MM-DD for a birthday or anniversary; YYYY-MM-DD for a trip (its first day) or an event.

year.description: A birthday’s or anniversary’s first year, so the line can say which one it is.

anyOf.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

end_date.description: A trip’s last day, on or after `date`.

place.description: A trip’s destination: "Zürich", or "Paris, Texas" to choose among cities of one name.

email.description: Remind in the morning email (and so in apps).

reminders.description: Days before to remind; by default 7, 1 and 0 (a trip 14, 1 and 0).

revision.description: Send it back to change or remove the date.

next.description: Its next date, or today while a trip is on.

through.description: A trip’s last day this time.

today.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

UpcomingBatch.description: At most 50 entries in all, and at least one.

added.description: In the order they were sent, with their ids.

unlocked.description: Badges this save earned, only while Show badges is on, and never on a replay.

from.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

through.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

days.description: Only the days with a reminder due.

date.description: A day in the account’s own time zone.

send_at.description: When that morning’s email is due, with the account’s offset that day.

next.description: The `before` for the next older page.

ActivityRow.description: One thing that happened. Each kind keeps its own fields (note.added has `day` and `note`, and from 1.6.0 `moment`, the kinds of a moment it came with; a reads row `calls` and `tools`); `via` says through what, and a token’s rows name it as `token` and, from 1.4.0, by id as `token_id`.

kind.description: Its family is one of mail, reads, note, transcript, description, import, badge, email, reminder, place, upcoming, settings, pause, status, signin, export, photo, address, calendar, connection, feedback, egg, account.

token.description: The name of the token it came through.

token_id.description: The id of the token it came through, as `GET /v1/me` gives it. Absent on rows written before 1.4.0, and on rows no token wrote.
